beats.text: Dawn light bled across the clearing as I stood in the sash, the mouth-band tight over my lips. My first time as Sacrificiant, the weight of my father's path pressing harder than the linen.
I breathed behind the cloth, tasting the morning chill and the sharper edge of fear that always came when an audience watched.
Seren knelt before me, spine straight from months of rehearsal, her eyes calm. I touched her shoulder once, a private reassurance no one else saw.
The presiding Dohkar called for the cost. Seren spoke her earliest memory aloud, voice steady, offering the small bright thing she had rehearsed.
At the edge of the gathering Julian stood motionless, the Provast whose office my father once held. My gaze found him before I could stop it.
Seren began the invocation. For those first words the rite felt simple, the words I knew better than I had ever spoken them.
Then she named the wish instead of the rehearsed one. She spoke my name and the loss I carried, her compassion offered for every witness to approve.
The misaligned words caught. The air split in a jagged line that reached for me, a tearing that would brand or break the Sacrificiant who stood too close.
The tear stopped mid-reach, arrested by nothing I could name. The clearing held its breath around the half-formed ruin.
The Dohkar named the bent wish and the residue still smoking in the air. He charged me with shaping the sacrifice and interfering in the rite.
My path to Dohkar, Chayr, Provast trembled under the public accusation. Even while it fell I felt Julian's stillness at the edge.
The assembly watched the residue and the Dohkar's finger pointed at me. What they had seen could be read as my interference.
Julian stepped forward from the edge. He said he could hear I was aligned with my own innocence.

beats.speaker: Julian
beats.text: I place The Answer in your hands so any misalignment will be plain.
He closed my fingers around the cool weight. The assembly watched him question me before them all.
His voice stayed low, intimate as an accusation. He asked whether I had called to him through the rite.
I felt the pull of his attention and the heat it carried, the same pull I had never named aloud.
The Dohkar's charge still hung over me. Julian's nearness made the clearing smaller.
I held The Answer that was never mine and waited for the next question.
The rite had not ended. Everything I wanted stood one answer away from ruin.

oasOpening.speaker: Julian
oasOpening.text: You shaped her wish through desire, hoping I would rescue you.

postInterruptionBeat.text: The Answer rested in my hands while the clearing waited for what came next.

temptation.action: Hold his gaze and step closer
temptation.dialogue: Ask what you truly want from me.

reversal.action: Turn the question back on him
reversal.dialogue: Why watch so closely if you fear me?

boundary.action: Draw hands back from The Answer
boundary.dialogue: This inquiry belongs to the Dohkar, not you.

confession.dialogue: I wanted you to see me.
